I've found myself playing quite a bit of Insurgency, so I thought I'd mention a few words about it.

It almost dubs itself as a realitic, tactical shooter, although I don't really feel like that's what it is. It's more like Call of Duty, with the bullshit cut out and tension added in. It's quite a nice mic. nsurgency focuses on close quarters combat (and being in the Source engine also probably adds to the fact that...) so there's no vehicles, so you'll have to go to Battlefield if you're looking for your action movie fix. I really enjoy the balance it has between realism and fun - it doesn't feel too realistic like ARMA, but not as arcade-y as COD, but it hasn't sacrificed the fun.

The game runs on a 'supply points system', but has each class designated a role. There's only a couple spots for snipers. If they're taken, though, you have to pick someone else. There's usually a few 'Assault' classes with rifles and SMGs. Once you're in your class, you only get a certain selection of guns to pick from based on that class. So for snipers, you can't pick SMGs. I think this system makes sense though, because you're picking a role, not a loadout with killstreaks and the best perks.

That said, it does have it's own problems. I don't really notice much 'personality' between the guns. Not a whole lot of recoil. I'm not sure whether that's to say you're playing as Big Boy Barry who knows how to fire continuously without sacrificing accuracy, but I'm occasionally making fuckups from randomly spotting the enemy in the corner of my vision and panicking XD. I'm enjoying the game though. Tension is whrere it really excels. Being the last one alove on a point has never felt so exhilirating, with throwing a stolen molotov in a doorway and your last smoke in the other.

It's multiplayer only, but being Source engine means it's relatively easy to set up a server, or like me, you can just hop into whatever you fancy. The game's still receiving periodic updates of maps and guns, and the community, somewhere around the 2k to 4k player count, seems small - but it's quite tight. I can imagine finding your own server you frequent to be a real breeze. It regularly drops on sale to around £4, and is well worth every penny.

7/10: A fun shooter, that has a number of different gameplay modes and can be picked up on the cheap. Once you've played a few hours, you've pretty much seen all there is, and the lack of a campaign may upset some. However, the multiple co-op modes leave open the option of hijacking an empty server and tag teaming with a few of your own buddies, and a quick training mode introduces you to the basic mechanics. The tension, also, is unparalleled. Not many FPS games go for tension, which is where Insurgency fills the void.

I picked up Insurgency in the winter sale. I wanted to purchase squad but for $40 it was a bit to much for me to grab. Insurgency quickly replaced CS:GO and Battlefield 2 for me. This quote sums it up quite nicely.

balance ... between realism and fun - it doesn't feel too realistic like ARMA, but not as arcade-y as COD, but it hasn't sacrificed the fun.

You can't go rushing in like a retard or you'll die, well unless you have an actual plan and are trying to ambush the enemy. Some modes you have to camp, it is more of a strategical element than a point element. The point mechanism rewards you for completing objectives versus killing. I've put about 20 hours into the game at this phostoint. It is a great game and at a great price.
